pick.headline: Gorbachev calls for democratization at the January plenum
pick.summary: On January 27, 1987, Mikhail Gorbachev opened a plenum of the Soviet Communist Party's Central Committee on cadre policy with a call for 'democratization': secret ballots and a choice of candidates in party and local elections.
pick.significance: The January plenum turned perestroika from economic repair into political reform. It began the opening of the Soviet system that led, within three years, to contested elections, to the end of the party's monopoly and to the loss of Moscow's hold on Eastern Europe.

alternates.headline: Freed hostages welcomed home in Washington
alternates.summary: On January 27, 1981, the 52 Americans released by Iran arrived in Washington and were welcomed by President Reagan at the White House.
alternates.significance: Reagan used the occasion to warn that future acts of terrorism against Americans would meet swift and effective retribution.

alternates.headline: Auschwitz marks fifty years since its liberation
alternates.summary: On January 27, 1995, survivors and heads of state gathered at Auschwitz-Birkenau to mark the fiftieth anniversary of the camp's liberation by the Red Army, with Polish President Lech Walesa as host.
alternates.significance: The commemoration was the first at Auschwitz held in a free Poland with the leaders of Germany and Israel present, and the planning was marked by disputes over how far the ceremony would name the Jewish victims who were the great majority of those murdered there.
